subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should backup startup cleanup delete stale OpenClaw-owned temp artifacts after age and live-owner guards, and should that cleanup include prior timestamped default/directory-output archive basenames?
rationale: The code blocker is mechanical, but the destructive cleanup policy is compatibility-sensitive and should be accepted intentionally before merge.

options.title: Fix Timestamped Matching First
options.body: Repair the matcher so documented backup flows are covered, then have maintainers accept the guarded cleanup policy before landing.

options.title: Accept Fixed-Basename Only
options.body: Maintainers could knowingly land cleanup for stable explicit output filenames and leave default/directory-output archive temps to a follow-up.

options.title: Pause Cleanup Policy
options.body: Pause or close this PR if startup deletion of stale backup artifacts needs a different recovery/debugging design.

recommendation.title: Fix Timestamped Matching First
recommendation.body: Repair the matcher so documented backup flows are covered, then have maintainers accept the guarded cleanup policy before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and refactored the original backup implementation and are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for backup cleanup policy.
